title: greater than and less than operators give incorrect result with abs
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in:
- Godot v4.7.rc1
- Godot v4.6.3.stable
- Godot v4.6.1.stable 
- Godot v4.4.stable.mono
- Godot v3.6.stable.mono.official [de2f0f147]
- Godot 3.0-stable

Not reproducible in:
- Godot 2.1.6-stable
- Godot 1.0-stable


### System information

Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 Ti (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.9186) - 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-12400F (12 threads) - 15.81 GiB memory

### Issue description

When comparing two equal values in gdscript where the one on the "greater" side is an absolute value that contains two values being added or subtracted the inequality is stated to be false when it should be true.

For example:
```gdscript
var i = 0.10+0.05
print(abs(i))
print(0.15)

print(abs(i) < 0.15)
print(0.15 < abs(i))
print(abs(i) > 0.15)
print(0.15 > abs(i))
```

prints:
```
0.15
0.15
false
true
true
false
```
The same issue exists when the equality is added (except now it is when the abs() is on the "lesser" side it shows false when it should be true):
```gdscript
var i = 0.10+0.05
print(abs(i))
print(0.15)

print(abs(i) <= 0.15)
print(0.15 <= abs(i))
print(abs(i) >= 0.15)
print(0.15 >= abs(i))
```
which prints:
```
0.15
0.15
false
true
true
false

```

It doesn't matter if the input to abs is a variable, two variables or written directly in it. It applies to both addition, subtraction and multiplication (I haven't checked any other operations). If there's only one value in abs() it works as it should from what I can see.

I was using Godot v4.6.1.stable when I discovered this, no custom build, modules, extensions or plugins.

N/A
